findings.title: Deprecated methods in candy machine UI
findings.description: The candy-machine-ui repository uses deprecated web3.js connection methods in src/connection.tsx, specifically getParsedConfirmedTransaction, getRecentBlockhash, and setSigners. These methods are deprecated due to improvements and changes in the web3.js library, and their use may lead to compatibility issues or unexpected behavior in future versions. The vulnerability arises from reliance on outdated API functions that are no longer maintained. An attacker could potentially exploit this by targeting environments where deprecated methods behave inconsistently or are removed, leading to denial of service or failed transactions. The impact is limited to functionality disruption rather than direct fund loss, but it undermines reliability and maintainability.

findings.title: Outdated dependencies in candy machine UI
findings.description: The candy-machine-ui project uses multiple outdated npm packages, some of which have known security vulnerabilities (including critical ones), as revealed by `npm audit`. The root cause is failure to update dependencies, leaving the application exposed to known exploits in older versions of libraries such as @solana/web3.js and @project-serum/anchor. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities through supply chain attacks, malicious payloads, or client-side exploits if the UI is compromised. The impact includes potential compromise of user sessions, wallet connections, or deployment integrity, though direct fund loss is not immediate. The presence of 32 vulnerabilities (8 critical) significantly increases the attack surface.
